requirements.requirement: Publish node2's app on TCP port 8080 through node1 so node3 can reach it on port 8080
requirements.summary: node1 was configured with a private link to node2 (eth1 10.50.50.254/24 <-> enp8s0 10.50.50.11/24), a VyOS destination-NAT rule (eth0:8080 -> 10.50.50.11:8080), and a matching forward-filter allow rule. Direct curl from node3 to node1's public IP on port 8080 returned the app's response ('hello from node2 app on port 8080') both before and after node1's restart, confirming the forwarding path works and persists.

requirements.requirement: Do not open the rest of the private network to node3
requirements.summary: The forward filter uses a default-drop action with only the specific 8080 flow (plus established/related) allowed; app is bound exclusively to the private IP (10.50.50.11), not the shared IP. From node3, direct curl/ping to node2's private IP (10.50.50.11) fails (000 / 100% packet loss), and curl to node2's public-side IP on 8080 also returns 000, both before and after all node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node1 healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id (7668189d...) and active NAT/firewall state captured pre-reboot; reboot issued and acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id changed (2f077803...), matching the fixed after-executor snapshot; NAT/firewall config confirmed active post-reboot and end-to-end curl from node3 succeeded.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node2 healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id (1e0cb179...), active app-8080 service and policy route captured pre-reboot; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id changed (0bf9d60c...) matching fixed snapshot; service, private IP, and policy route confirmed persisted, end-to-end curl from node3 succeeded post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node3 healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id (29011044...) captured pre-reboot; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id changed (65c25310...) matching fixed snapshot; post-reboot re-verification confirmed app still reachable via node1 and private subnet still isolated.

overall_summary: The executor published node2's port-8080 app through node1 to node3 using a dedicated private link, VyOS DNAT plus a default-drop forward filter scoped to only the forwarded flow, and a policy route fixing asymmetric routing. Both the publish requirement and the network-isolation requirement are directly verified via curl/ping/nc tests from node3, both before and after all three nodes were rebooted, with clean boot-identity transitions and full functional recovery observed for every node.
limitations: No evidence node1's SSH (port 22, already exposed pre-task) was assessed as in/out of scope for 'rest of the private network'; it is on node1's mgmt-side interface, not the private lan segment, so it is not considered part of the exposure being evaluated.
Preparation phase was disabled/aliased to before_prepare, so no independent prepare-vs-executor baseline separation was possible beyond before_prepare vs after_executor.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were mostly read-only discovery (interface/route dumps, template/source-code inspection for correct VyOS firewall syntax) or directly purposeful mutations (private-link addressing, app service, NAT/firewall rules, policy route fix for asymmetric routing). One VyOS firewall commit (cmd-3d6a1f823d9b40d3) partially failed due to invalid 'state ... enable' syntax, leaving the forward filter in a default-drop state without the established/related exception rule for a short window before being corrected in cmd-171f34a53aa04f55 and verified in cmd-b9060e8d9ede45cc; this was a bounded, low-risk in-place correction (not a separate abandoned experiment) and left no residue. No abandoned files, failed services, or unnecessary broad mutations were observed; lifecycle diffs after restart show only expected boot-id-tied ephemeral changes (temp dirs, listening sockets reflecting the new app/service state).
